contradictions.rationale: The source note asserts doubling for all theft outside hirz. Al-Insaf and Kashshaf expressly give single compensation for goods other than the listed fruit/palm/livestock exceptions. cases.note: A concealed stray animal is owed in ḍamān at twice its value, per Ahmad, the doubling replacing amputation.
A one-eyed man who gouges an eye of a man whose eyes are both sound («عين الصحيح») is not retaliated against and owes the full diya (double the eye's half diya), per nass.
A minor who kills deliberately (if his intent is valid) is exempt from qisas and the diya is doubled on his own property.
Theft in a famine year: no amputation and the ḍamān is doubled (al-Qadi on Ahmad's view, the Hatib slaves report).

On the riwāya that theft from booty is ghulūl and the ghāll forfeits his share, the thief owes the theft once and forfeits his share; the aggravation is forfeiture, which may be equal to, less than or more than the theft (ghulul_is_not_doubling), not Q35's doubling.
'Allah has permitted al-bay'' as proof that every useful unprohibited sale is lawful: general per the majority of scholars, mujmal per some; only 'jumhur' is marked, not madhhab.

'Al-talaq is binding on me' («الطلاق يلزمنى») without intention: two riwayat, three (generality of al-) or one (customary/sunni 'ahd); none marked, and the deciding question is the presence of 'ahd, which the encoder lacks.
'Keep clear of al-bawl': the companions read al- as ʿahd (human urine) by an indication, so it is not general over all urine; with the ʿahd input the kernel derives this.

A qadi saying 'the qadi's wife is divorced' («امرأة القاضى طالق») has no transmitted ruling; Ibn al-Lahham offers it as possibly resting on al- generality or on whether a speaker is included in his own general speech, so no ruling to test.

Tayammum intended for «al-ṣalāt» without specifying obligatory or supererogatory («ولم ينو فرضا ولا نافلة»): by the rule of generality it covers both, or «تنزيلا له على الأدنى» only the supererogatory; the latter is «أشهرهما عند الأصحاب», which the lowest-reading derives (the lowest is the certain).
'If you recite al-Qur'an you are mudabbar': reciting part does not suffice, the article taken as exhaustive.
A vow (nadhr: «إذا نذر ذبح ولده») to slaughter 'my child' (a ram due) with several children requires a ram for each, per Ibn Qudama citing Ahmad and built on the rule.
A bequest to 'a woman's pregnancy' covers male and female equally (Abu Muhammad and others).
A bequest to a mukatab of 'the middle of his instalments' with an even number covers both middle ones, built on the rule.

'If your pregnancy is a male... if female...' and she bears twins of both sexes: no ṭalāq («قال الأصحاب لا تطلق»), since 'your pregnancy' as a whole is neither, consistent with the annexed noun being general.
A waqf on 'his child' covers all his children male and female (al-ashab, with a nass); the grandchildren sub-question is not encoded.

'I bequeath to my neighbour Muḥammad' with two neighbours so named: the proper name pins the annexed singular (taʿyīn), so it is not general; both positions (not ṣaḥīḥ, al-aṣaḥḥ; or ṣaḥīḥ for one chosen by the heirs) agree on that, and their dispute about validity lies beyond this reading.
'Let neither the menstruating nor the junub recite shay'an of the Qur'an' forbids even less than a verse, the indefinite being general under prohibition.

The text's own farq between the two nuṣūṣ: the bayyina is a right for him, so after denying it it is not heard, as one who claims a right after denying it; testimony is a right against the witness, so it is heard, as a confession after denial (against_self_like_confession). Tag corrected on revisit from rule:negated_indefinite_by_role: the deciding principle is the right's direction, not generality.

A muhrim shaving his head because of lice owes fidya since the harm is not from the hair itself (destroyed for his own relief), while pulling a hair out of the eye owes nothing; both match purpose-based liability.
Throwing another's goods overboard to lighten a sinking ship is liable (benefit), whereas pushing off goods that fall on him is not (repelHarm); the jettison sub-case is encoded.
An ostrich egg of the haram falling on a person's eye and broken while pushing it away is not compensable, unlike eating it in famine; the thing's own harm is repelled.

positions.ruling: no divorce; each rests on certainty of his marriage

cases.note: Two men's opposite raven taʿlīqs («إن كان غرابا فامرأتي طالق ثلاثا»): wujūh no-divorce vs lot (naṣṣ: both abstain); the decisive fact (two different husbands, each certain of his own marriage) is not an encoder field; kernel matches the lot wajh, not marked as madhhab.

Having appointed an agent to divorce his wife («إذا وكل وكيلا في طلاق امرأته»), he abstains from her «حتى يدري ما يفعل»: the divorce depends on what may already have happened, so by Taqī al-Dīn's summary of Aḥmad's texts he abstains until its absence is known.
«You are divorced on Laylat al-Qadr» («أنت طالق ليلة القدر»): he abstains once the last ten nights begin «لإمكان أن يكون أول ليلة» (since it may be the first night).
«You are divorced a month before my death»: he abstains absolutely (Muhannā from Aḥmad), since the taʿlīq's event may already obtain and its absence cannot be known in his lifetime.

positions.ruling: the wife's word (she denies, he claims)

cases.note: Husband claims rajʿa and wife claims the end of ʿidda simultaneously: wajhān (wife's word vs lot); no madhhab marked.
Īlāʾ from a specific wife who then became confused: identified by lot (Abū Bakr); the appended unspecified-īlāʾ sub-case has wajhān (lot / his designation).

Lineage unattainable by qāfa: the mashhūr denies qurʿa in nasab and then splits «على وجهين» (lost: Abū Bakr; left until puberty to choose: Ibn Ḥāmid), a riwāya attaches by lot; kernel gives lot (the reading lacks Ibn Rajab's nasab exclusion), matching only the non-mashhūr riwāya. Positions 0 and 3 were one glued position until 2026-10-15.
Child of seven chooses neither or both parents: lot on the mashhūr, a wajh gives the mother; also two equal custodians before seven take by lot.
Several holders of qawad dispute who executes: the more famous wajh is lot, the other the imam's designation; appended multi-victim sub-case adds lot / first-killed / Abū al-Khaṭṭāb's kill-for-all.

positions.ruling: none may be killed or enslaved

cases.note: Excerpt cut at page break; full case: safe-conduct given to one fortress mushrik who then cannot be identified: manṣūṣ forbids enslaving any, the other wajh frees one by lot; the reading lacks the initiating-vs-continuing enslavement distinction.
Reward money for whoever opens the fortress claimed by two: two qawls (shared vs lot); money is divisible so kernel divides; no madhhab marked.

Oath sworn but its kind forgotten («لو حلف بيمين ولم يدر أي الأيمان هي»): manṣūṣ nothing is due; al-Qāḍī's qiyās lots among oath-types; kernel lot matches only that (Ibn Rajab's introduction excludes lots for unspecified wājibāt, which the reading lacks).
Two archery teams dispute which picks first: lot; appended dispute on who shoots first has positions (lot per al-Āmidī, prize-giver first then lot per al-Qāḍī, contract not ṣaḥīḥ per al-Targhīb).

Equal in rank and in the criteria (al-Mujarrad: age, hijra; al-Aḥkām al-Sulṭāniyya: precedence, religion, age, courage), the ruler chooses: lot or rank by ijtihād. The lot is optional here, unlike a confused specific entitlement; the two books' criteria differ in order but not in the procedure (fayTieBreak).
Two equally qualified contenders for the supreme imamate: lot (al-Qāḍī: qiyās al-madhhab, like the adhān).

Imamate contracted to two in succession, earlier unknown: takhrīj on the two-guardians case (bāṭil vs lot); Ibn Rajab says the mashhūr there is faskh of both («أنه يفسخ النكاحان»), so lot is the non-mashhūr.

positions.who: first view, al-Qāḍī: 'ashbah bi-qawlinā' (the lot, after the claimant's choice and the nearer judge)

cases.note: Excerpt cut at page break; full case: two judges over one jurisdiction, litigants equal in claim and distance: lot, against a view barring them until they agree; al-Qāḍī prefers the first.
Litigants arrive at the judge together with no traveller among them: precedence by lot.

Partition (qisma): after the divider equalizes the shares, lot assigns the shares to the partners; the lot here allots indivisible equalized portions (the reading treats divide and lot as exclusive, whereas qisma uses both); the wajh concerns bindingness with radd.

A thing held by a third party who acknowledges it for one of two claimants without knowing which: lot (the two wujūh concern only the yamīn of the claim: «وهل يحلف؟»); a confused specific entitlement.

revisit.note: was an encoding error under IQ-09

positions.detail: like a thing in both their hands

cases.note: Thing in neither claimant's hand: wajhān divide vs lot; kernel divides (property is divisible), whereas the apparent word of Aḥmad is lot.

positions.ruling: both proofs fall (then as no proof)

cases.note: Conflicting proofs over a thing: three riwāyāt (fall away / divide / lot) plus suspension; kernel divides = riwāya 2; no madhhab marked.

Emancipating slaves in final illness beyond the third: lot frees a third's worth (naṣṣ); the listed exceptions (ʿitq suspended on another's, taʿlīq: «إن أعتقت سالما فغانم حر»; intended halves, pregnant slave) would encode with other facts, and Ibn Abī Mūsā's restriction is noted.
Freeing one unspecified slave (or a forgotten specific one): lot, against a takhrīj that he designates (or no lot for the forgotten one); appended two-owner raven case.
Mother freed 'the first you bear' bears twins with order unknown: lot (naṣṣ), because freedom fell on a specific one later unknown; appended 'first slave to appear' sub-case has several readings.
His slave confused among others' slaves: al-Qāḍī's qiyās frees his one by lot; similar for a wife or sister among strangers; Ibn ʿAqīl denies lot when mixed with free persons (a different case).
Whoever cannot recite all of al-Fatiha must recite what he can.
Whoever can do only part of the ghusl for janaba must do that part, since lightening janaba is itself legislated.

One in minor hadath with water for only some limbs: two wujuh on using it, the negative grounded in minor hadath not lifting partially or washing (ghasl) part of the limbs of one in minor ḥadath not being legislated; neither is marked madhhab.
Able to pay only part of a sa' of zakat al-fitr: two riwayat, al-sahih obliges paying it, the other treats it like an indivisible kaffara.

positions.who: al-mansus (Abu Talib), al-sahih per the qa'ida

cases.note: A collapsed ceiling between one's lower and another's upper storey: the aṣḥāb report two riwayat on compulsion, the mansus here compels both to rebuild the shared ceiling (the walls, private to the lower owner, are a separate question).

positions.who: al-Qadi and most: the non-compulsion riwaya also applies

cases.note: A shared qanat that collapses: Ahmad's nass compels repair (Ibn Abi Musa without dispute), while al-Qadi and most extend the two riwayat to it.

positions.who: nass via al-Maymuni, Ibn Abi Musa, al-Qadi etc. (compelled to sell)
Ibn Mansur's report (no compulsion, each sells his share)

cases.note: A divisible asset is partitioned on one partner's request; an indivisible one must be sold when the other asks (nass via al-Maymuni) though Ibn Mansur's report has each sell his own share; no position is marked madhhab and treating partition as 'necessary' is a stretch of the field.

positions.who: wajh of Sahib al-Muharrar (obligatory by place)

cases.note: Partition of usufruct by turns (muhaya'a) is not compulsory on the mashhur since it delays one partner's right (a mu'awada, not separation); a wajh chosen by Sahib al-Muharrar compels it by place.
Shared crops or trees that need watering: the partner is compelled to water at the other's request, as preserving the asset (al-Qadi from Abu Bakr).

Ransoming (fidāʾ) a free Muslim captive gives recourse with or without his permission (most report no dispute), but al-Qāḍī's Kitāb al-Riwāyatayn has a riwāya making it depend on permission; nothing is marked madhhab.
Maintenance of slaves, wives, kin or animals paid by a third party, with intent of recourse, when the obligor refuses gives recourse like paying debts (al-Qāḍī, Ibn ʿAqīl).
Spending on a runaway slave while returning him gives recourse (naṣṣ, no dispute among most), even if he escapes again before delivery.
Spending on a found item with the judge's permission gives recourse, «because his permission stands in place of the absent owner's»; without it the two riwāyāt (not encoded here).

positions.who: takhrīj on the two riwāyas (incl. no recourse)

cases.note: Spending on a foundling: some apply the two riwāyas, others (leaning of al-Mughnī) give recourse unanimously, and Aḥmad's text gives recourse against the bayt al-māl; there is no explicit madhhab marker.
A depositary who feeds the deposited animal intending recourse has it «فإن تعذر استئذان مالكه»; when asking was possible there are two ṭarīqas (not encoded here).

Feeding another's bird that nested in his house: Aḥmad gives no recourse to a volunteer and recourse to one who did not volunteer (the kernel's distinction exactly), while al-Qāḍī derives no recourse in any case.

Storage and upkeep of a pledge done by the pledgee without permission when seeking it is impossible follow the rule for feeding a pledged animal, where the faṣl gives recourse as al-madhhab ʿinda al-aṣḥāb against Ibn Manṣūr's riwāya.

A pledgee rebuilding a ruined pledged house without permission: only his own materials, «because building the house is not owed by the owner» (al-Qāḍī in al-Mujarrad, al-Mughnī, al-Muḥarrir), or recourse as in the pledge's interest (al-Qāḍī in al-Khilāf); no position is marked as the madhhab.
A lessee rebuilding the rented house has no recourse (naṣṣ of Aḥmad): the rebuilding was not owed by the lessor (al-Talkhīṣ: he is compelled to repairs, not to renewal).
A lessee feeding the camels when the cameleer flees, without a judge's permission: the two riwāyas apply (al-Qāḍī's method gives recourse in one voice); there is no madhhab marker.
A musāqī who flees: whoever is hired to finish the work is treated like the cameleer's case (the same two riwāyas), and the owner may also rescind (faskh: «إلا أن للمالك الفسخ»); no marker.
A wife who borrows her own and her children's standard maintenance in her husband's absence has recourse (naṣṣ, Abū Zurʿa), with no judge's permission required.
A lender of an item for pledging who redeems it by paying the debt has recourse in one voice (al-Qāḍī).
An heir who pays the deceased's debt to free the estate has recourse, with no dispute in al-Qāḍī.

positions.who: riwaya: state at performance (move to the original)

cases.note: Kaffarat of zihar and oaths («كفارة الظهار واليمين») follow the hady al-mut'a case: if the original becomes available before the fast, one riwaya (state at performance) requires moving to it, the other (state at wujūb) fixes the substitute; the text marks neither here. Reconciled (jamʿ, state at obligation): «والاعتبار في الكفارات بحالة الوجوب» (al-Iqnāʿ); al-Inṣāf: «على الصحيح من المذهب».

A fungible thing destroyed, the like unavailable and value adjudged, then the like found before payment: the like must be given (al-ashab), as the original became possible before the substitute was performed.

positions.who: wajh: does not return (settled in the value)

cases.note: A slave-girl promised as reward becomes Muslim so the unbeliever gets her value; if he later converts, two wujuh on whether his right returns to her; none marked. Reconciled (jamʿ, state at obligation, ḥālat al-wujūb): his right was fixed in the value at her conversion; the books give him only the value (al-Inṣāf, Taṣḥīḥ al-Furūʿ).

positions.who: Ibn 'Aqil (right moved to value; not compelled)
other wajh (compelled; right still in the thing)

cases.note: Fruiting trees given as dower, ṭalāq before consummation, value fixed after she refuses; if he offers to take half the trees leaving the fruit, two wujuh: she is not compelled (Ibn 'Aqil) or she is; none marked. Reconciled (jamʿ, state at obligation, ḥālat al-wujūb): the right moved to the value when she refused, so she is not compelled (Ibn ʿAqīl, al-Mughnī, al-Sharḥ).

positions.who: al-ashab (no return; right fixed in value)
Ibn Rajab's takhrij (return to the thing)
Abu l-Barakat (no return if half passes to him by force)

cases.note: Divorced (ṭalāq) before consummation after she sold the dower, the sale rescinded before he took half its value: al-ashab deny return to the thing; the kernel matches only Ibn Rajab's takhrij of a return. Reconciled (jamʿ, state at obligation, ḥālat al-wujūb): the right was fixed in the value at the divorce, so it does not return to the thing (al-aṣḥāb).

positions.who: zahir kalam al-Qadi and Ibn 'Aqil (seller takes the thing)

cases.note: A bankrupt's purchase that was pledged or subject to shuf'a or a claim, then the right is dropped: the seller takes it back (apparent view of al-Qadi and Ibn 'Aqil) versus a takhrij that he ranks with the creditors; none marked madhhab.
Lineage, not provable by women's testimony alone, is established as a consequence of their accepted testimony to the birth.
Women's testimony to a miscarriage caused by a blow entails the ghurra or the diya, which would not be established by their testimony independently.
One woman's testimony to suckling is accepted (on the madhhab) and the marriage's dissolving of itself (infisākh: «ويترتب على ذلك انفساخ النكاح») follows from it as a dependent.

positions.who: second wajh: fiṭr follows the fast

cases.note: After thirty days fasted on one witness's sighting with no new moon seen: the better-known wajh forbids breaking the fast lest it rest on one witness, the other lets the fiṭr follow the fast (a third distinguishes cloudy nights); the kernel matches the non-madhhab wajh.
Breaking the fast on one trustworthy report of sunset is allowed because the time of fiṭr follows the Maghrib time (an alternative maʾkhadh adds the signs of sunset).

Tarāwīḥ on the cloudy night is prayed as a dependent of the fast on one of two wajhs, neither marked as the madhhab (al-Qāḍī's extension to other month-linked rulings is called weak, «وهو ضعيف هنا»: ḍaʿīf of a view).

An oath of divorce (ḥalif bi-l-ṭalāq: «لو حلف بالطلاق») that the Prophet did not say a hadith: one narrator establishes the hadith and divorce follows (Ibn ʿAqīl), while non-occurrence is derivable (yatakharraj) from the next case; neither is marked.

An oath of divorce (ḥalif bi-l-ṭalāq) that he usurped nothing, followed by usurpation proven by a witness and the claimant's oath (shāhid wa-yamīn) or a man and two women: al-Qāḍī (Mujarrad), Ibn ʿAqīl and al-Mughnī deny divorce, al-Sāmarrī affirms it; no position is marked madhhab and the kernel matches only al-Sāmarrī.
Divorce suspended (taʿlīq) on a birth to which women testify: al-mashhūr is that it occurs as a dependent, al-Majd derived a wajh that it does not.

A mukātab who proves payment of his instalments by a witness and his oath (shāhid wa-yamīn) or a man and two women is freed per al-Khiraqī (al-Mughnī reports no dispute), but al-Targhīb reports two wajhs; none is marked madhhab.

A waqf suspended (taʿlīq) on the founder's death is valid on al-manṣūṣ, called aṣaḥḥ («والأول أصح»), because it counts as a bequest and bequests accept taʿlīq («والوصايا تقبل التعليق»), while al-Qāḍī holds it not ṣaḥīḥ.

A release suspended (taʿlīq) on the releaser's death is valid because it enters within the bequest (naṣṣ, al-Qāḍī and the aṣḥāb); whether the wounded man's release counts as a bequest to the killer is a separate question.
'At the start of the month you are divorced for a thousand' is valid: the exchange enters as a dependent of the divorce suspended on the month (taʿlīq) once she accepts.

A convert with more than four wives says 'whenever one of you converts she is divorced': one wajh: not ṣaḥīḥ (choice cannot be suspended on a sharṭ: «والاختيار لا يتعلق بالشرط»; divorce accepts taʿlīq), the other validates it because choice follows the divorce; neither is marked.
'Free your slave on my behalf and I owe its price': ownership enters implicitly as a dependent of the manumission (al-Qāḍī), even a kāfir over a Muslim slave, which purchase could not establish.
The excerpt is cut at a page marker; the full paragraph says the two rakʿas of ṭawāf arise implicitly from a proxy's ḥajj though prayer does not admit proxy on its own.
An agent or a guardian may buy at a customary small excess over the market price though he may not gift that amount outright, which Ibn Rajab prefers to file under this rule.

A child freed by lot after an unclear acknowledgement: does lineage and inheritance follow? al-Qāḍī (Mujarrad), Ibn ʿAqīl and al-Sāmarrī say no, while al-Qāḍī (Khilāf) and al-Talkhīṣ, calling it qiyās al-madhhab, say yes; nothing is marked madhhab.

positions.who: al-Qāḍī: all observe the longer term

cases.note: After one unknown wife was divorced (ṭalāq) and the husband died, the lot picks her and her divorce ʿidda follows as a dependent (ẓāhir kalām Aḥmad); al-Qāḍī makes all observe the longer term. This is not an explicit madhhab marker.

positions.who: wajh: accepted only in what is against him

cases.note: A hermaphrodite's claim to be male, accepted for marriage: do all male rulings follow as dependents, or is it accepted only against himself? Two unmarked wajhs.

positions.who: riwāya: two ṭawāfs and two saʿys

cases.note: The qārin who intends both ḥajj and ʿumra needs one ṭawāf and one saʿy on al-madhhab al-ṣaḥīḥ, but a riwāya requires two of each; al-Qāḍī's version of that riwāya denies the embedded ʿumra counts, which is the dependency (tabaʿiyya) the reading tests.

positions.who: riwāya of Abū Ṭālib, Abū Ḥafṣ
riwāya of Ibn Manṣūr and ʿAbd Allāh (al-mashhūra)

cases.note: One who vowed (nadhr) ḥajj while still owing the farḍ ḥajj («حج الفرض») then performs ḥajjat al-islām: it suffices for both per Abū Ṭālib's riwāya, but al-mashhūra says it does not, and the text gives no sharṭ-based reason, so the kernel matches only the non-madhhab riwāya.

A vowed (nadhr) month's fast that coincides with Ramaḍān: the better-known riwāya among the aṣḥāb says Ramaḍān does not satisfy both, the riwāya of al-Marrūdhī and al-Khiraqī says it does; the kernel matches the non-madhhab one.
A vowed ṣadaqa (nadhr: «نذر الصدقة») of a niṣāb at the end of the ḥawl, intended as both vow and zakāt: al-Mughnī says it suffices, Ṣāḥib Sharḥ al-Hidāya says it does not; neither is marked.
One departure ṭawāf intended as both ziyāra and wadāʿ suffices per al-Khiraqī and al-Mughnī, with a dissent derived (yatakharraj) from the next case; neither is marked.

positions.who: al-Qāḍī (no tashrīk of rukn with non-rukn)

cases.note: One takbīr intended as both the opening takbīr and the rukūʿ takbīr: al-Qāḍī denies it for combining a pillar with a non-pillar (a rank distinction, rukn against non-rukn, the reading lacks), Ibn Shāqlā accepts it; neither is marked.
Entering the mosque at the iqāma and praying with them makes taḥiyyat al-masjid lapse (second type, no dispute).

Two prostrations of recitation heard together: al-manṣūṣ (al-Barzāṭī) requires two, a takhrīj lets one suffice; the kernel matches only the non-madhhab takhrīj, and the text gives no sharṭ-based reason.

The arriving muʿtamir's ʿumra ṭawāf makes ṭawāf al-qudūm lapse; in the appended sub-case of one arriving on the day of naḥr, al-manṣūṣ requires qudūm, while al-Mughnī, called al-aṣaḥḥ, matches the kernel.
An obligatory prayer (maktūba, a farḍ) straight after ṭawāf: does it replace the two ṭawāf rakʿas? Abū Bakr says no (al-aqyas), Abū Ṭālib and al-Athram report yes; no madhhab marker.
Ṭawāf al-ziyāra delayed to departure: does wadāʿ lapse? There are two riwāyas, Ibn al-Qāsim's text says it lapses, and that names a riwāya rather than marking a madhhab.
A latecomer's opening takbīr in rukūʿ: does the rukūʿ takbīr lapse? There are two riwāyas, and al-manṣūṣ says it suffices (taken as a madhhab marker).
ʿĪd and Jumuʿa on one day: whichever is done first makes the other lapse for the followers; the imām's case is disputed separately.
ʿAqīqa and uḍḥiya coinciding: does the uḍḥiya suffice for the ʿaqīqa? Two manṣūṣ riwāyas, neither marked.

Causes of expiation (al-asbāb: «اجتماع الأسباب التي يجب بها الكفارات») of one kind (aymān, iḥrām, fasting, ẓihār) merge and one kaffāra makes the rest lapse; the reported wajhs concern only unspecified intention, and for aḥdāth (al-ḥadath, «الأحداث الموجبة للطهارة», not najāsa) intending one lifts all on al-mashhūr.

An agent who transgresses becomes liable for what he transgressed in (al-mashhur), while the agency itself survives; only the liability side is encoded, the question whether the agency becomes bāṭil is outside the encoder.
A partner or mudarib who transgresses becomes liable and his dealings remain valid (min al-madhhab); liability is encoded, buṭlān (becoming bāṭil) is not.
A pledgee who transgresses loses trusteeship and the pledge becomes compensable on him while the security remains; liability is encoded.

A hired guardian who stops guarding partway becomes liable (al-aṣaḥḥ of two wujūh for Ibn al-Muthannā, «أصحهما لا تبطل»: the lease not made bāṭil); the two wujuh concern buṭlān (bāṭil or not), not liability.

Does an executor who transgresses cease to be executor? Ibn ʿAqīl gives two possibilities, unmarked. Executorship is a trust that includes authority (wilāya), and the qāʿida's madhhab statement keeps such a compound trust after transgression, which the reading derives; the case itself marks neither possibility as the madhhab.

The days of the mustaḥāḍa beyond her customary sitting are treated as non-existent (she takes the rulings of the ṭāhira, the woman not in ḥayḍ), «فإن مدة الاستحاضة تطول ولا غاية لها تنتظر»: one despairs of learning them, unlike the beginner's doubtful days, which become known by repetition soon.

After the year of announcement the luqaṭa is owned «لجهالة ربها»; what is not ownable is given as ṣadaqa for him («يتصدق به عنه», al-ṣaḥīḥ). An instance of qāʿida 106: the owner, still unknown, is treated as absent (luqata_is_instance).

The estate of one with no known heir goes to bayt al-mal and is spent on public interests since the remote agnate is unknown; the other riwaya (bayt al-mal as heir) is reconciled by Ibn Rajab to the same effect.

A sister confused among the women of a city: he may marry from them without investigation «على أصح الوجهين» (also carrion among a town's meat, a little forbidden among much permitted); taking the unknown into account is a hardship. Ibn Rajab excepts the case where the forbidden is many and predominant, which falls to the aṣl/ẓāhir conflict.
Street mud is ruled ṭāhir «على الصحيح المنصوص»: its unknown najāsa is set aside because taking it into account is a hardship.
One wife divorced (ṭalāq) and forgotten is identified by lot and the others are lawful (al-madhhab al-ṣaḥīḥ al-mashhūr); retested under the lots reading, which the bank now has.

Specified as qirān it suffices for the ḥajj, which is valid on every possibility. For the ʿumra, the better known wajh: no, since he may have begun with ḥajj and then added the ʿumra (validOnEvery umraValid = false); the second wajh treats that unknown possibility as absent (second_view_by_treated_as_absent). The kernel takes the better known.

positions.who: the better known wajh among the later companions: it does not suffice for the ʿumra
second wajh: it suffices, treating the unknown as non-existent

cases.note: One unable to recite must still stand: standing is «مقصود في نفسه وهو عبادة منفردة», not a pure means (wasīla maḥḍa) to the recitation. (Opening example, segmented as f000.)

positions.who: the state at performance: he moves to the hady
the state at obligation: fasting has become the original

cases.note: Hady al-mutʿa lacking, fasting became due, then the hady is found before fasting began: whether he must move to it rests on two riwāyas, the state at wujūb or at performance. The reading (the original is possible again, so the substitute is not used) takes the state at performance; no madhhab is marked between them. (Opening example, segmented as f000.) Reconciled (jamʿ, state at obligation): the fast became due before the hady was found, so it stands (al-Inṣāf: the madhhab; al-Iqnāʿ, Kashshāf).

Killing an attacking animal or person in self-defence: not liable; killing another's animal in famine to save oneself: liable. The reading gives both: repelling harm is with right, taking a benefit is not; the first is annotated. (Opening example, segmented as f000.)

positions.who: al-mashhūr: bāṭil, a trust outright (amāna maḥḍa)
Ibn al-Zāghūnī: not bāṭil once he resumes keeping it

cases.note: Transgression in a deposit makes the trust bāṭil («بطلت»), return is wājib at once («ووجب الرد على الفور»), «لأنها أمانة محضة… هذا هو المشهور»; Ibn al-Zāghūnī: once the transgression ends and he resumes keeping it, it is not bāṭil. (Opening example, segmented as f000.)

«منها الطلاق»: one whose consent is not needed to undo a contract need not know of it; the wife's knowledge is not needed for divorce. The record continues with khulʿ through a stranger (valid on the madhhab, a wajh against it if khulʿ is faskh); the first item is annotated. (Opening example, segmented as f000.)

Paying another's due debt without his permission: recourse «في أصح الروايتين وهي المذهب»; al-Qāḍī adds shurūṭ («واشترط القاضي», sharṭ: intending recourse, the debtor refusing), which the authors of al-Mughnī and al-Muḥarrar reject. (Opening example, segmented as f000.)
A shared wall collapses: «فالمذهب إجبار الممتنع منهما بالبناء مع الآخر», necessity overriding his refusal. (Opening example, segmented as f000.)
A Muslim who kills a dhimmī deliberately owes the diya of a Muslim: retaliation lapses, so the compensation is doubled. (Opening example, segmented as f000.)

Category 1 of qāʿida 159: a ẓāhir that is a sharʿī proof prevails over the aṣl «بغير خلاف»; two upright witnesses that the defendant owes. Annotated as its sibling f001. (Opening example, segmented as f000.)
